title: ÆTHER: Storm Entry v2 (scored to the script, plan mode)
maker: ElevenLabs Music API on the owner's paid plan

positive_global_styles: a mass hero ENTRY film score scored to picture, written like today's biggest Tamil and Telugu film composers: goosebumps, swagger, a theatre-roaring moment
about 112 BPM felt as a heavy half-time swagger, a dark minor raga with a sharp fourth and chromatic bends, a whistle-able 5-note hero hook with Carnatic gamakam slides on every lead

half real instruments played close, natural and dry (nadaswaram, thavil, violins, low brass, temple bell), half fresh electronics (thick dark synth bass, gritty bent synth lead, thunder booms, rain on a tin roof as the hi-hat, a dragged iron chain as percussion)
deep wordless male crowd chants and shouts answering the hook, no lyrics
very loud, punchy, clean, dark, low-mid heavy cinematic mix

positive_local_styles: the very first sound: a huge thunder crack with a deep cinematic boom, then only heavy rain ticking on a tin roof, no music yet
one temple bell rings alone in the rain, then a low menacing synth bass creeps in underneath, the villain's world, dark and still

a dragged iron chain scraping on stone becomes a slow walking pulse; a gritty bent synth plays a rising 3-note call (root, minor third, fifth, last note bent up) and hints the hero hook low; tension rising
tension builds under the chain pulse, then a reversed veena swell rises into one massive full-band hit with a deep boom and a huge crowd shout 'HEY!' on the last beats
the swagger groove slams in: heavy half-time drums, thick synth bass, the 5-note hero hook on the gritty synth lead, wordless crowd chants answering every phrase
halfway through a real thavil joins, played natural and dry, like an old festival drummer starting to play again
a duel: a real nadaswaram and the synth lead trade the hero hook, every phrase answered by a punching band stab, the phrases get shorter and faster, the thavil doubles time
the whole band stops dead: one beat of total silence with only the rain, then a single raindrop
BANG: the biggest slam, the hero hook a whole step higher with the full band, a frenzied wedding-drum ketti melam roll on thavil, crowd chant on every accent, violins in Indian-style unison
the hook in its grandest form on brass and nadaswaram, then pulled down into a heavy half-time stomp, menace and power held back

a korvai: one rhythmic phrase played three times by the whole band, landing on a massive final hit with a thunder boom and sub drop, then the 3-note call alone on the synth and one temple bell ringing over the rain

brief.notes: Jithesh 30 Oct 08:03 on Storm Entry v1: 'really good, but we missed a proper script'. New rule 17: script first, then score. v2 is scored beat by beat to the scene script (music/storm-entry-v2/storm-entry-script.md, copied in 'script'), so every instrument enters for a story reason. storm-entry-v2 = composition plan, one section per script beat; storm-entry-v2p = the same script in prompt mode (music_v2). We measure which one lands the beats.

story: The hero's first appearance: he walks into a village temple festival the villain has silenced, in a storm, and gives the village its festival back.
human_work: to be added by the owner: melody, take choice, edits, mix
